llm.relevance_to_user: 该综述总结了短柄全髋关节置换术后假体周围骨重塑的临床证据，但未涉及有限元建模或接触力学分析。
llm.why_not_core: This is a clinical review summarizing bone remodeling outcomes from DEXA studies, not a biomechanical modeling paper; it does not report stress/strain distributions, micromotion values, or contact mechanics from finite element analysis.

summary_zh.motivation: 总结短柄全髋关节置换术后假体周围骨重塑的临床证据。
summary_zh.method: 系统综述短柄THA术后DEXA测量的骨密度变化文献。
summary_zh.result: 短柄设计可减少近端应力遮挡，但骨重塑模式因柄设计而异。
summary_zh.validation: 基于已发表临床研究的DEXA数据汇总，无建模验证。

summary_en.motivation: To systematically review clinical evidence on periprosthetic bone remodeling following short-stem total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: A systematic review of DEXA-measured bone mineral density changes in short-stem THA studies.
summary_en.result: Short-stem designs reduce proximal stress shielding, but remodeling patterns vary with stem design.
summary_en.validation: Summary of published clinical DEXA data; no finite element or experimental validation.

papers.title: Reconstructed and analyzed X-ray computed tomography data of investment-cast and additive-manufactured aluminum foam for visualizing ligament failure mechanisms and regions of contact during a compression test
papers.abstract: Three stochastic open-cell aluminum foam samples were incrementally compressed and imaged using X-ray Computed Tomography (CT). One of the samples was created using conventional investment casting methods and the other two were replicas of the same foam that were made using laser powder bed fusion. The reconstructed CT data were then examined in Paraview to identify and highlight the types of failure of individual ligaments. The accompanying sets of Paraview state files and STL files highlight the different ligament failure modes incrementally during compression for each foam. Ligament failure was classified as either "Fracture" (red) or "Collapse" (blue). Also, regions of neighboring ligaments that came into contact that were not originally touching were colored yellow. For further interpretation and discussion of the data, please refer to Matheson et al. (2017) [1].

summary_en.motivation: To visualize and classify ligament failure mechanisms in open-cell aluminum foams during compression using X-ray CT.

summary_en.result: Ligament failures were categorized as fracture or collapse, and new contact regions were identified.
summary_en.validation: Experimental compression testing with CT imaging.

papers.title: Lattice Structure: Modeling, Design, and Simulation
papers.abstract: An algorithm for designing and optimizing homogeneous lattice structure to support given load condition is presented. The approach is to homogenize the safety factor distribution by altering trusses parameters defining the lattice structure. The algorithm combines theoretical mechanics in the initial design section, and FEA method to optimize and verify the tests result. The Octahedral lattice structure is utilized as an example of the design and optimization algorithm. The initial design decides the lattice structure node locations, and the optimization process redistributes structure material to reach higher strength without adding or removing material at the whole structure level, this means each truss may have a different cross-section due to their functions. Modern additive manufacturing technology made the fabrication of such lattice structure to be possible. The reference parameters in optimization iterations are Safety Factor distribution and the Von-Mises stress. Material stress limit and design safety factor are determined outside the iteration loops. The optimized lattice structure and the traditional lattice structures are physically tested in an MTS compress test machine. The result for a 3×3×3 octahedral cells lattice structure shows the optimized lattice structure support 60% more load than the traditional homogeneous lattice structure at the same weight. The optimize/design algorithm could be applied to other lattice structures formed by nodes and or general structures.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及晶格结构的设计优化与力学测试，与AM生物医学方向相关，但未涉及应力遮挡或骨整合。
llm.why_not_core: No link to stress shielding or stiffness matching for biomedical implants; no fatigue testing; no surface roughness or osseointegration characterization.

summary_zh.motivation: 设计优化均质晶格结构以提升承载能力。
summary_zh.method: 结合理论力学与有限元法，通过调整桁架参数优化安全系数分布。
summary_zh.result: 优化后的晶格结构比传统结构承载能力提高60%。
summary_zh.validation: 通过MTS压缩试验验证优化效果。

summary_en.motivation: To design and optimize homogeneous lattice structures for improved load-bearing capacity under given loading conditions.
summary_en.method: Combined theoretical mechanics and FEA to homogenize safety factor distribution by altering truss parameters, with iterative optimization.
summary_en.result: The optimized octahedral lattice structure supported 60% more load than the traditional homogeneous design at the same weight.
summary_en.validation: Experimental compression tests on 3D-printed lattice specimens using an MTS machine.

papers.title: Actively Engaging Students in Culture, Gender, and Class Issues in Medieval Literature
papers.abstract: Students often find it difficult to understand literature of another era and a world that differs from their own. From interacting with illuminated manuscript pages to conducting a mock trial, this article discusses ways in which visual and active learning techniques can be used to engage students in medieval literature and culture.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文与有限元代理建模、生物力学或植入物设计完全无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is about pedagogy in medieval literature, with no computational modeling, FEA, surrogate modeling, or biomedical context.

summary_zh.motivation: 帮助学生理解中世纪文学中的文化差异。
summary_zh.method: 使用视觉和主动学习技术，如手稿互动和模拟审判。
summary_zh.result: 提高了学生对中世纪文学和文化的参与度。
summary_zh.validation: 无实验验证，仅为教学讨论。

summary_en.motivation: To help students overcome difficulties in understanding medieval literature from a different cultural context.
summary_en.method: Employed visual and active learning techniques including interaction with illuminated manuscripts and mock trials.
summary_en.result: Enhanced student engagement with medieval literature and culture.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation; purely pedagogical discussion.
